summary: Task grill of quality-gate-baseline: four cold-read rounds before delegation, plus a fifth after the contract was corrected mid-implementation. Every finding was stall-class or falsification-class. The fifth round was necessary because the worktree's .factory was mirrored at task start, so contract updates made in the main repo never reached the worker — it correctly refused an unsatisfiable contract three times (S-0007/S-0008/S-0009) rather than fake a green. Decision: KEEP as one task. A further four rounds ran after the contract was corrected in the worktree, each finding a verified defect in shipped code rather than a contradiction introduced by the previous round: a test suite broken two independent ways, a ledger path outside write scope, harness-owned workflows that must never be formatted, and an ignore list that would have become a permanent exemption for the very next task.
gaps: The recorded task had three acceptance criteria but only two differently-worded plan_contracts; the recorder requires exact three-way equality and would have refused the contract before delegation
package-lock.json was outside the write scope, so installing ESLint and Prettier would have exceeded the delegated scope
Root typecheck runs build:contract, which EMITS rather than checking, so FACTORY_TYPECHECK_CMD could satisfy its name without giving the no-emit guarantee
Lint scoped to src/ would have skipped contract/test/**, which ships, and tools/quality-gate.test.mjs, which belongs to no workspace
The guard test proved only that a referenced npm script exists, so FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD="npm run build" would satisfy it and make verify.py green while linting nothing

The gate was not self-protecting before harness-wiring: the guard was outside FACTORY_TEST_CMD and no CI ran root verification, so a later edit could repoint or delete the quality command and still pass everything

The remediation boundary was undefined: 'resolve whatever the gate reports' contradicted 'configuration and scripts only', and the vendored tree's explicit any usages and console suppressions meant an unspecified ruleset could either demand broad rewrites or be weakened until it reported nothing
Prettier has no workspace extends convention, so 'one root config both workspaces extend' was unimplementable as written, and no configuration owned the root-level tools/ test
The required-test command omitted decision 0009's mandatory canonical form (TS_NODE_PROJECT and --require ts-node/register); a .mjs test does not exempt it
CI as specified omitted npm ci and explicit Node/Python setup, so ESLint, Prettier and TypeScript binaries would not exist in a clean Actions checkout

Write scope named four whole directories (backend/, contract/, tools/, .github/) while the plan forbade source remediation and unrelated workflow changes — broad enough to permit exactly what it prohibited

The exclusion shape was unspecified: a directory-wide .prettierignore entry would permanently exempt future backend and contract code, breaking the half of the criterion that requires all new code to be format-checked

The guard pinned FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD -> quality -> lint && format:check but not the BODIES of root lint and format:check, so repointing root lint at `echo lint` would leave the declared mapping and the guard green while ESLint never ran

The criterion claimed 'configs' are linted and format-checked, but the globs named workspace TypeScript and tools/ only, leaving eslint.config.mjs, .prettierrc.json, the package.json files and quality.yml outside the gate — and .envrc is shell, which neither ESLint nor Prettier parses
@eslint/js was installed during the host-side unblock but the ESLint config did not use it — an unjustified dependency under conduct §9
The CI workflow ran on both push and pull_request, duplicating verification for branch pushes with no stated benefit

The backend test suite could never go green: branding.identifiers.test.ts resolves backend/src and contract/src from the repo root while the workspace script runs with cwd=backend, so it searched backend/backend/src

The same suite also failed with TS7006 implicit-any errors across pre-existing test files, because ts-node/register type-checks while backend/tsconfig.json deliberately excludes tests from typecheck scope
A clean checkout has no contract/dist, so every @3f/contract import failed with TS2307 unless the structural build runs before typecheck and test
plans/deferrals.md was outside the write scope although the contract requires D-0005 and D-0006 ledgered, so stage-done would have failed the seal after all the work was complete

The .github workflows factory-scaffold.yml, gardener.yml, harness-health.yml and roadmap-gate.yml all fail Prettier and are harness-owned — forge upgrade replaces them wholesale, so a blanket .github/**/*.yml glob would have blocked the gate on files we must not format

The D-0006 ignore list would have become a permanent exemption: Prettier ignores whole FILES, and the list contains the exact files api-surface-trim edits next, so new lines written there would evade the 'all new code is format-checked' claim
42 backend tests across 8 files need a migrated Postgres app DB, which CI has no way to provide, so the contracted verify:ci could never be green

The guard checked git diff HEAD and untracked files only, so once a later task COMMITTED a change to an ignored file, CI would see a clean tree and that file would stay exempt from Prettier permanently

The guard read only fully-quoted exports while verify.py accepts unquoted ones and takes the LAST assignment, so appending `export FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD=true` would leave the guard green while local verification ran `true`
quality.yml declared no permissions block, inheriting the repository's default GITHUB_TOKEN scope, and pinned its actions to mutable version tags
frontend-foundation is contractually required to widen the quality gate but its scope excluded eslint.config.mjs and tools/quality-gate.test.mjs — it would have blocked exactly as this task did
contradictions: BLOCKER: backend/src/atlasTokens.test.ts reads frontend/app/globals.css at import time and throws, because decision 0006 excluded the vendored Pulse frontend and no frontend/ exists — so FACTORY_TEST_CMD could never have been green, and the task's own acceptance criterion was unreachable

BLOCKER: the CI acceptance criterion was impossible as written — verify.py requires an approved plan from the git-local .git/forge/run.json, which a fresh CI checkout does not have, and the only ways through (fabricating factory state, or patching verify.py) are forbidden by vendor integrity

verify.py PREFERS a pre-set FACTORY_* environment variable over .envrc, so a CI override would silently bypass the declared gate while everything reported green — the plan's guard did not account for this
The manual verification claimed bad spacing would fail both lint and format-check, contradicting the plan's own syntax-only ESLint policy under which spacing is a Prettier concern alone
Reviewer focus accumulated across rounds until it simultaneously required CI to run verify.py and to run the product aggregate instead

The worktree's .factory contract was mirrored at task start and never carried the S-0007/S-0008 scope resolutions made in the main repo, so the worker was reading a contract that simultaneously demanded format:check pass over all vendored source and forbade both reformatting and exclusion
resolutions: acceptance_criteria and plan_contracts[].statement are now the same three exact strings
package-lock.json is in write scope and the ESLint/Prettier packages live in root devDependencies
FACTORY_TYPECHECK_CMD invokes both workspaces' own tsc --noEmit; emitting stays in the structural/build command

One root flat eslint.config.mjs covers backend/src, contract/src, contract/test and tools/; tools/quality-gate.test.mjs is both linted and format-checked; contract/test remains outside the tsconfig includes and unrunnable, which stays deferred under D-0002

The guard resolves the named npm scripts to their BODIES and asserts the pinned graph (structural = build + both integrity checks; typecheck = both workspaces no-emit; quality = root lint + format:check; tests = backend suite + the guard), so a substring dodge like `echo lint` fails

The guard is inside FACTORY_TEST_CMD, and this task creates .github/workflows/quality.yml running the aggregate on every push; harness-wiring only widens that same workflow for the frontend and re-proves it

The ESLint ruleset is pinned conservative and syntax-only, with an explicit hard stop: anything beyond trivial mechanical fixes to pre-existing source becomes a separately planned task rather than hiding inside a baseline
One named root .prettierrc.json GOVERNS both workspaces by being what the scripts point at, rather than by a non-existent extends mechanism
The required-test command uses decision 0009's canonical form verbatim
CI pins Node 20 and Python 3.11, runs npm ci, then npm run verify:ci, and sets no FACTORY_* variable
Write scope narrowed from four directories to eleven named files plus the one ledgered deletion

backend/src/atlasTokens.test.ts is REMOVED — not skipped and not glob-excluded, since a temporarily-excluded known failure is the exact false green this gate exists to prevent — ledgered as D-0005, with frontend-foundation owning equivalent 3F token coverage
CI runs the product-owned npm run verify:ci aggregate over the same four command bodies, needing no factory state and touching no harness machinery
CI sets no FACTORY_* variable and the guard asserts that, closing the env-override bypass

Negative controls are now one per tool and distinct: a parse/obvious-error violation fails ESLint but not Prettier; formatting-only drift fails Prettier but not the syntax-only ESLint policy; and all three mapping failures fail the guard
reviewer_focus was rewritten from scratch rather than appended to again, removing the verify.py/aggregate contradiction

.prettierignore lists the EXACT pre-existing files (~70, generated with prettier --list-different) under a header naming D-0006, never a directory wildcard; the list is self-liquidating and new paths stay checkable
The guard asserts the command graph RECURSIVELY down to every runnable leaf — root lint, root format:check, and each workspace's own lint/format:check body

The criterion and plan now state coverage honestly: format-check the JSON/YAML/MJS config files this task adds and lint the executable MJS, while .envrc is validated semantically by the guard rather than claimed to be covered by tools that cannot parse shell

The dependency set is eslint, prettier, typescript-eslint and @eslint/js — the last ADOPTED deliberately by human decision: eslint.config.mjs builds on js.configs.recommended as its base with typescript-eslint layered for TS parsing
The CI workflow triggers on push only
The corrected contract and task plan were re-recorded INSIDE the worktree via the recorders, and this grill is bound to that worktree plan digest
The test invocation is corrected scripts-only to run with the repo root as cwd; test bodies are not edited

Tests run transpile-only — type checking belongs to FACTORY_TYPECHECK_CMD and these files are deliberately outside it, so type-checking them in the runner duplicates a gate and blocks on debt the hard stop bars remediating; the resulting absence of any type coverage for test files is ledgered as D-0007
The aggregate orders the structural build before typecheck and test
plans/deferrals.md is in the write scope

The four harness-owned workflows are excluded in .prettierignore under their own header naming forge upgrade as the reason, kept separate from the D-0006 product-source list; the format glob targets only the config files this task adds

The .prettierignore header carries a binding precondition — before any task edits a listed file it formats that file and removes it from the list in the same change, and any new entry requires a named dated deferral — enforced mechanically by the guard, not merely documented

FACTORY_TEST_CMD and CI run test:hermetic only; the DB-backed set is demonstrated evidence on the host (human decision, D-0008), split by declared file lists rather than a silent glob so a new DB test must be classified deliberately
The guard pins a baseline content hash for every D-0006 path; a changed hash fails until that path leaves .prettierignore and the normal glob covers it

The guard implements verify.py's effective-assignment semantics and rejects any FACTORY_* whose final effective value is not the pinned command, with negative controls for later, unquoted and duplicate exports
quality.yml declares permissions: contents: read and pins every action to an immutable commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment
frontend-foundation's contract now owns eslint.config.mjs and tools/quality-gate.test.mjs and carries an explicit criterion to widen the gate to three workspaces
open_items: NON-BLOCKING: the approved story plan's T9 says harness-wiring will 'add or adjust' product CI, while this task creates the workflow. 'Adjust' covers the real division of labour (T5 creates, T9 widens for the frontend and re-proves), so the story plan was NOT reopened for a wording nuance — reopening it would invalidate the human's approval and every downstream digest. Recorded here instead.

NON-BLOCKING: stopped at four rounds under the same human direction that stopped the requirements loop. Each round here was stall- or falsification-class rather than refinement, but the loop was not run to a clean round.

NON-BLOCKING: verify.py's preference for pre-set FACTORY_* environment variables is a general bypass affecting every task's local verification, not just this one. Closed for CI here; worth an upstream harness note.

NON-BLOCKING: the cancelled round-5 requirements Codex job still shows as a dead entry in the launch ledger. `forge codex` exposes only `status`, no stop, so `forge next` will keep advising a re-run that is deliberately not happening.

NON-BLOCKING: orchestrator error, recorded so it is not repeated — `forge task start` mirrors .factory at creation, so contract edits made in the main repo afterwards do not reach the worker. Update the contract inside the worktree, and note the harness's own tip: record the task grill LAST, immediately before approve/stage-start, since committing outside .factory/ and plans/ re-stales it.
NON-BLOCKING: D-0007 records that backend test files are now type-checked by nothing — excluded from tsconfig and run transpile-only. Previously true in practice, now true by design.

NON-BLOCKING: the remaining findings are IMPLEMENTATION work the contract already requires — the recursive guard, the two .prettierignore headers with content-hash pinning, exact CI trigger and permissions pinning, linting eslint.config.mjs, and the test:hermetic/test:db lists. They are unbuilt because the worker blocked on contract defects before reaching them. The task grill evaluates the contract AND the current implementation, so it cannot converge until the worker runs; the three-lens autoreview is the gate on whether it built them correctly.

NON-BLOCKING: D-0008 records '42 tests'; the eight DB-backed files actually contain 50 test leaves. The boundary (which files are host-only) is correct; the count in the deferral text is not. Correct it when the declared test:db list lands.

NON-BLOCKING: the guard should fail on an UNCLASSIFIED backend test — one in neither test:hermetic nor test:db — so the split cannot silently drift. Implied by the contract's 'explicit list, never a silent glob'; left to implementation and the autoreview rather than another contract cycle.
current_flow: Today: .envrc declares no FACTORY_* command, so verify.py silently skips the quality gate; backend and contract have no ESLint or Prettier config; root typecheck emits rather than checking; the backend suite throws at import on an absent frontend CSS file; and no CI runs verification on push.

criteria_map.the .envrc declares FACTORY_STRUCTURAL_C: The four variables declared with the pinned script graph, and tools/quality-gate.test.mjs resolving each named script to its body to assert that graph (so `echo lint` or `npm run build` fails). Proven by `python3 factory/scripts/verify.py` green with four commands executed and none skipped, plus the guard's three mapping negative controls. Depends on removing backend/src/atlasTokens.test.ts (D-0005), without which FACTORY_TEST_CMD can never be green.
criteria_map.FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD covers every workspa: npm run verify:ci runs the same four command bodies without factory state, and .github/workflows/quality.yml (created by this task) pins Node 20 + Python 3.11, runs npm ci, then the aggregate on every push, setting no FACTORY_* variable. Proven green on this task's own PR.
criteria_map.backend and contract have ESLint + Prett: One root eslint.config.mjs (backend/src, contract/src, contract/test, tools/) and one root .prettierrc.json the scripts point at. .prettierignore enumerates the ~70 pre-existing vendored files under a header naming D-0006 — an explicit self-liquidating list, never a directory wildcard, so every new path stays checkable. Format checking also covers the JSON/YAML/MJS configs this task adds; the executable MJS is linted too. .envrc is shell and is validated semantically by the guard, not claimed as ESLint/Prettier coverage. Proven by `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` green, each failing on its own distinct negative control (parse error fails ESLint not Prettier; formatting drift in tools/ fails Prettier not the syntax-only ESLint policy; the same drift in an excluded vendored file does NOT fail, which is the ledgered exclusion working). The harness-owned .github workflows (factory-scaffold, gardener, harness-health, roadmap-gate) are excluded under their own .prettierignore header because forge upgrade replaces them wholesale, so the format glob targets only the config files this task adds.

new_abstractions: npm run verify:ci — a product-owned aggregate over the same four FACTORY_* command bodies, so CI can prove the identical gate without the factory run state verify.py requires. Justified because the alternatives (fabricating .git/forge/run.json in CI, or patching verify.py) both violate vendor integrity.
tools/quality-gate.test.mjs — a guard asserting the SEMANTICS of the four commands rather than their names, because the name alone is satisfiable by any script and would make the gate decorative.

rounds.question: During the host-side unblock I installed `@eslint/js`, but the worker's ESLint config doesn't use it. Conduct §9 says an unused dependency has to be justified or dropped. Which way?
options: Adopt it as the base ruleset (Recommended)
Remove it, keep the config minimal
rounds.chosen: Adopt it as the base ruleset (Recommended)
